title: The Christine Collins Story
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the 1928 disappearance of nine-year-old Walter Collins in Los Angeles and the case of his mother Christine Collins. After Walter vanishes, the LAPD later presents a boy as Walter; Christine insists he is not her son, and Captain J.J. Jones has her committed to a psychiatric ward. A runaway, Arthur Hutchins Jr., is revealed as the impostor. Sanford Clark later says he and Gordon Stewart Northcott murdered boys including Walter; Northcott and his mother Sarah Louise Northcott are linked to the Wineville Chicken Coop murders. Christine sues the LAPD, wins a judgment never paid, testifies at Northcott's trial, and visits him before his execution, where he denies it. The episode also covers the 2008 film Changeling, its fictionalized elements, and a listener mail about rewilding and indigenous long-term stewardship.

segments.title: Opening banter and Changeling movie talk
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the true crime episode, mention a parole update on a past case, and discuss the 2008 Clint Eastwood film Changeling, noting its dramatic license.

segments.title: Walter Collins disappears and the LAPD context
segments.summary: Walter Collins, nine, disappears in March 1928 in Los Angeles. His mother Christine is a single mother whose husband is in prison under another name. The hosts describe the LAPD's recent embarrassment in the Marion Parker kidnapping and early search leads.

segments.title: Early leads and the search
segments.summary: Tips include a gas station worker's sighting and a suspicious foreign-looking couple. Walter's father suggests an enemy from prison; the lead goes nowhere. Five months pass without progress.

segments.title: Boy returned from Illinois and Christine refuses him
segments.summary: Police say they found Walter in Illinois. At the juvenile detention center Christine says the boy is not her son. Captain J.J. Jones gaslights her, and she eventually agrees to take the boy home to try him out.

segments.title: Dental records and Christine's commitment
segments.summary: Christine finds evidence such as dental records and teacher testimony that the boy is not Walter. Jones charges her with being a bad mother and has her committed to a state hospital against her will for six days.

segments.title: Arthur Hutchins Jr. confesses; Sanford Clark's claims
segments.summary: Arthur Hutchins Jr., a runaway, is exposed as the impostor through handwriting. Sanford Clark, nephew of Gordon Stewart Northcott, claims Walter was murdered. Christine goes public, a grand jury hears her, and the Police Commission takes no disciplinary action against Jones.

segments.title: Lawsuit, Northcott trial, execution, and Changeling differences
segments.summary: Christine sues the LAPD and Jones and wins, but is never paid. Northcott is convicted of murders at the Wineville chicken coop; he sends Christine a telegram claiming he lied, then denies it at San Quentin before his hanging. The hosts note film changes, such as the invented ending, and the town renamed afterward.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: A listener mail from Paul, chief technology officer at Mossy Earth, about rewilding and indigenous long-term stewardship, followed by the sign-off.
